VERDICT: AGREE on reviewable head f55b72da05a0c8ed8031c53ddb70badb17f3c6aa (raw branch tip 358fba1102b77d1b429948c56cd40b2e5c1a1d14, whose only change is proof/-only and therefore skipped by resolve_reviewable_head). No blocking defect found. This PR's diff is docs+proof only (HANDOFF.md, proof/lwb-recut-73-stale-disagree.json); every quantitative claim in the PR body and in HANDOFF.md that I could check, I checked, and all of them hold.

WHY reviewed_commit IS NOT THE RAW TIP. The dispatch instructing this review said to record "the FULL head sha". Taken literally that would be 358fba11, which would make this record STALE ON ARRIVAL and unblock nothing: _review_ok compares reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head(), which skips commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. 358fba11 is proof/-only, so the reviewable head is its parent f55b72da. I reviewed the content of the full tip including 358fba11; f55b72da is the sha the gate is defined against and the sha whose content is under review. This is not relabelling an identifier to make a gate pass -- it is naming the sha the gate actually specifies, and I am stating the reasoning here rather than silently choosing.

So that line is genuinely re-derived, and it tolerates exactly ONE merge landing on main before it goes stale (see the queue-wide note below); that one-merge tolerance is measured here, not assumed.

RED CI IS THE REVIEW GATE ITSELF, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS PR. At review time all 6 `test` matrix jobs on 358fba11 were failing while the other 12 check runs were green. I did not take that at face value in either direction. GitHub's job-log blobs are blocked by this environment's proxy, and the check-run annotations only said "Process completed with exit code 1" at misleading workflow line numbers (.github:15, .github:91) which pointed me at the two lwb-env-leak steps. That attribution was WRONG and I caught it before writing it down: the per-step conclusions from the Actions jobs API show the ONLY failing step in every one of the 6 jobs is step 21, `lwb-lanes`, with steps 11 and 12 (lwb-env-leak and lwb-env-leak-history) both SUCCESS. I reproduced the lwb-lanes failure locally: `lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 74` reports all three commits touching a shared path with 0 independent reviews in reviews/74/, needing 1. reviews/74/ did not exist. That is precisely what this record supplies, so this PR should go green on the push that lands it. NEAR-MISS RECORDED per the honesty rules: I nearly filed a finding against the env-leak steps on the strength of annotation line numbers alone.

THE PROOF RECORD IS HONEST ABOUT ITSELF. proof/lwb-recut-73-stale-disagree.json sets checked_by to the literal "pending-independent-reviewer-routine" rather than inventing a reviewer identity, lists its self-authored/unchecked status under `unproven`, and reports every `tokens` field as "unknown: not measured from a session transcript in this run" instead of fabricating numbers. Its `pr` is 74, matching its directory-authoritative PR. I specifically checked for the failure shape where a record reads one field and ignores a sibling that changes the meaning, and for a scoped claim dressed up as repo-wide; found neither in this diff.

RESIDUAL ORDERING FRAGILITY (non-blocking, NOT a defect in this PR). The PR's fix is to regenerate the block in the same commit that adds the proof record (f55b72d). A LATER commit, the tip 358fba1, then edits proof/lwb-recut-73-stale-disagree.json again to fill in the `pr` field -- so strictly speaking the generator is not the last write on the branch, the shape I was told to hunt. I tested rather than assumed: the generated block derives only a proof-record COUNT and an all-proven/outstanding split, neither of which depends on the `pr` field, so the tip edit is genuinely inert with respect to the block, and lwb_check_state_claims.py passes at the tip (verified directly, above). No finding. Worth knowing for the next re-cut: this branch is safe because of WHAT the last write changed, not because the generator ran last.

QUEUE-WIDE HAZARD THIS PR INHERITS (non-blocking, already flagged to the owner on #45, not fixable from inside this diff). This PR's generated block pins `main SHA: 0d1be71` and `24/24 proven`. Per probe P3 the main-SHA line accepts live main or live main's first parent, so it survives exactly one merge landing on main and reds out on the second; the proof-count line reds out as soon as a merge changes the count. Every open PR that edits HANDOFF.md shares this, which serialises the queue. Mentioning it so it is on the record for #74 specifically; it is not a reason to withhold AGREE.

LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES is a repository secret, unset in my environment, and the script correctly fails closed as UNCONFIGURED rather than passing while scanning for nothing. So my local run is "could not check", NOT "checked and clean". I rely on GitHub's own step conclusions (both SUCCESS in all 6 jobs) for these two gates, which is a different and weaker thing than my having measured them.
- scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute: not run. It is continue-on-error in CI and its digests are not expected to reproduce off the recording machine.
- The `commands` array inside the new proof record: I did not re-execute its recorded argv list or re-derive its digests; I independently re-ran the same test suite and gate scripts instead and got matching results.
- #64's diff, and the diffs of #51/#53/#62/#66/#68/#71: not audited. I verified only their open/green/reviewed STATUS, which is all HANDOFF.md claims about them.
- The Windows and macOS matrix legs: I measured only on this Linux container; for those I rely on GitHub's step conclusions.
- The `_review_ok` verdict-before-staleness ordering defect that this PR deliberately leaves out of scope: I did not attempt to fix or fully audit it. I did read it (line ~760 of scripts/lwb_lanes.py) and confirm the PR's characterisation is accurate -- the verdict!="AGREE" branch sets rejection_kind "other" and returns before the staleness comparison -- so a DISAGREE on a superseded commit is indeed unclearable in place. Deferring it to its own scoped PR is the right call and I agree with the PR body's reasoning, but treat that as a reviewer's opinion, not a measurement.
- Repository settings, rulesets, and merge-queue configuration: out of my authorisation and not inspected.
